summary.headline: HUDCO H1 FY27: disbursements above INR35,000 crore (up ~37%), loan book up 29% to INR1.86 lakh crore, net NPA 0.04%.
summary.overview: Management reported strong H1 FY27 growth: disbursements above INR35,000 crore, sanctions above INR1 lakh crore, and loan book up 29% to INR1.86 lakh crore. Net profit rose 31% and revenue from operations rose 26% on a half-yearly basis, with gross NPA around 0.7% and net NPA 0.04%. Management said spreads are about 1.96% (ex the INR20,000 crore low-yield GoI loan) with NIM about 2.93%, and reiterated 2% spread and 3% NIM targets, while flagging near-term repricing pressure from higher borrowing costs. The call also covered first PPP sanctions (about INR9,000 crore, Dharavi redevelopment yet to disburse) and RBI Upper Layer NBFC classification.

segments.name: Lending - sovereign / GoI loan
segments.commentary: INR20,000 crore loan to Government of India carries about 40 bps spread; repayment expected in FY2028-29, after which spread and NIM are expected to rise to about 2% and 3%.

segments.name: PPP / private lending
segments.commentary: About INR9,000 crore of PPP sanctions (slum redevelopment incl. Dharavi, HAM road projects, one renewable energy project); no PPP disbursement yet except Dharavi, expected to start in Q3.

segments.name: PMAY / housing
segments.commentary: Cumulative PMAY 1 and 2 sanctions about INR58,000 crore, releases about INR48,000 crore; state counterpart funding demand is uncertain as states prefer SDLs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 internal disbursement target INR65,000 crore; about INR30,000 crore remaining after H1.
FY27 loan book target about INR2 lakh crore; FY30 target INR3 lakh crore retained (management did not indicate a revision).
Spread targeted at about 2% and NIM at least 3% on a year-to-year basis, with possible temporary slippage from resets and market moves.
Negative credit costs (reversals) expected for a year or two given provision coverage around 95%.
About INR35,000 crore of ECB borrowing at around 6.5%-6.75% expected before the RBI swap window closes on 31 December; targeting slightly more than $3 billion under the window.
15 bps MCLR increase and ECB impact expected to reflect in Q3 FY27 results; about INR20,000 crore of loans to reset in H1.
capex_capacity: Around 1 lakh square metres of space to be created in next three years for asset monetisation; income expected from it.
Strategic business group being set up; regional offices being strengthened for post-sanction monitoring.
Sanctioned PPP pipeline long gestation (3 to 5 years), so disbursement conversion will be slow.
Overall sanctioned pipeline estimated at INR3 lakh crore to INR4 lakh crore; about INR1 lakh crore sanctioned each half-year.
demand_pricing: Management expects urban infrastructure demand to be large (World Bank estimate about INR250 lakh crore requirement by 2050, as cited).
Loan repricing on tranche-wise one-year reset tied to quarterly-revised MCLR; some states moving to quarterly reset.
Management said borrowers will pass higher costs through at reset; yields expected to rise over next two quarters.
Bond yields around 8% over last two to two and a half months; Q1 FY27 bonds of about INR2,200 crore raised at roughly 7%-7.25%; bank funding around 7.25%; no bond issuance in Q2.
PMAY 2 sanctions around 20 lakh units; government target 40 lakh units this year.

qa_highlights.question: How will yields and margins hold up over next one to two years as growth continues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assured about 2% spread at year-end and NIM at least 3%, with temporary slippage possible from resets and disbursement timing; current spread 1.96% and NIM 2.93% including the INR20,000 crore low-yield GoI loan.

qa_highlights.question: Will the currency translation losses continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX translation loss is zero this quarter and no losses foreseen; ECB maturities about five years and new FX exposure covered under RBI swap window; small FCNR portion maturing 2028 hedged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 disbursement target?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target INR65,000 crore; INR35,000 crore done in H1, INR30,000 crore remaining; target to be revised only if project pace accelerates.

qa_highlights.question: How are PPP sanctions and pipeline progressing; cost of borrowing by source?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR9,000 crore PPP sanctioned with Dharavi disbursement expected this quarter; sanction pipeline INR3-4 lakh crore. ECB blended cost about 6.75% after hedging on $2 billion raised; bonds about 8% currently; banks about 7.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in maintaining 2% spread given no relief in cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited RBI swap window borrowings at about 6.5%-6.75%, INR20,000 crore resets in H1, 15 bps MCLR hike, and moves to quarterly resets; said yields will rise over next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI Upper Layer classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly additional compliance; exposure norms of 25% and 5% (board approval) are not a constraint given loan book size; no material impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on ROA and credit costs?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA targeted at 2%-2.2%; negative credit costs likely for one to two years due to reversals with 95% provision coverage.

risks_watch: Spread compression risk: cost of funds elevated (bonds around 8%) and repricing lag; management expects margin recovery after FY28-29 GoI loan runs off.
Dependence on RBI swap window for cheaper ECB funding; about INR35,000 crore intended before 31 December.
Recovery of about INR1,200 crore in stressed assets under NCLT/DRAT, mostly private sector; timing uncertain.
PPP lending: risk premium rising, limited disbursement so far, state counterpart funding under PMAY uncertain.
Compliance requirements under RBI Upper Layer NBFC classification.
Negative credit cost may be unsustainable beyond one to two years; watch reversal pace.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and spread targets, but cautious on cost of funds and repricing; several answers were hedged ("temporary slowdown" possible) and key numbers such as revenue and profit growth were stated as percentages without absolute values.
key_quotes: Our gross NPA has declined to around 0.7%, and net NPA is just above zero, that is 0.04%, and we are committed to become zero Net NPA company very shortly.
I can assure you and the investors fraternity that our spreads will be around 2%, and we will be maintaining on year-to-year basis.
Going forward, we don't foresee any losses on foreign currency movement.
Since they have long gestation periods starting from the three years to the five years of the time, so the conversion will take some time regarding the disbursement and the loans.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.why: No physical plant or branch capacity additions were discussed; only ~1 lakh sq m of asset-monetisation space over three years and PPP gestation of 3-5 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 disbursements above INR35,000 crore against FY27 internal target of INR65,000 crore, with loan book targeted at about INR2 lakh crore from INR1.86 lakh crore (about +8%) and sanctions of about INR1 lakh crore per half-year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex or capacity expansion was not discussed beyond asset-monetisation space; utilisation is not a relevant metric for a lender.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not indicate revising the FY27 INR65,000 crore disbursement or INR2 lakh crore loan book targets; revision only if project pace accelerates.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged possible temporary spread slippage from resets and market moves, with bonds around 8% versus ECB at about 6.5%-6.75%, and the swap window closes 31 December.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First PPP disbursement (Dharavi) expected in Q3 from about INR9,000 crore of PPP sanctions, but no new product launch was specifically guided.

rows.label: Borrower repricing pass-through of higher costs
rows.why: About INR20,000 crore of loans reset in H1 and a 15 bps MCLR increase reflects in Q3 FY27, with management saying yields will rise over the next two quarters against bonds around 8%.

rows.label: ECB borrowing under RBI swap window
rows.why: About INR35,000 crore of ECB at about 6.5%-6.75% is expected before the window closes, targeting slightly above $3 billion, which should cap funding costs.

rows.label: Negative credit costs from provision reversals
rows.why: Provision coverage around 95% and gross NPA about 0.7% (net NPA 0.04%) support reversals for one to two years, though sustainability is uncertain.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement growth, asset quality and the 2% spread and 3% NIM targets, but cautious on cost of funds, repricing lag and PPP timing; analysts pushed on how spreads hold up without relief in funding costs.
